title: Sing, All Ye Nations, to the Lord
description: Sing, All Ye Nations, to the Lord in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 8 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 66, part 1, headed “Governing power and goodness; or, Our graces tried by afflictions”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Sing, all ye na-tions, to the Lord, Sing with a joy-ful noise; With mel-o-dy of sound re-cord His hon-ours, and your joys.

lines: Sing, all ye nations, to the Lord,
Say to the power that shakes the sky,
Come, see the wonders of our God,
In Moses' hand he puts his rod,
He made the ebbing channel dry,
There did the church begin their joy,
He rules by his resistless might:
Provoke th' Eternal to the fight,
O bless our God and never cease;
He keeps our life, maintains our peace,
Lord, thou hast prov'd our suffering souls,
So silver bears the burning coals
Thro' watery deeps and fiery ways
Led to possess the promis'd place

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. FLAVIAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
